Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the current rollout evidence—including both required 3D wake views—before touching the policy. I’ll also use the fish-control bookshelf at the required decision point and record any actual transfer in the prescribed note block.

The parent is already a successful capture controller, so this is a refinement problem, not a rescue. I’m comparing the four completed variants on arrival, distance integral, load, joint limits, and wake topology; the small scalar-score spread alone is not enough to choose the edit.

The evidence now supports a specific gap: bidirectional recovery removes speed-stop contact and beats the unguarded score, but its posterior-to-anterior channel can inject work based only on “anterior positive power,” which does not prove that the receiver is in the matching carrier phase. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a mechanism-level way to gate that transfer using joint-state phase, not for gain tuning.

The selected candidate will add one bounded mechanism: a normalized yaw-load gate on only the discretionary cross-joint work transfer. The baseline traveling carrier, target-course steering, soft acceleration envelope, speed guard, and angle barrier remain untouched; at low load the parent behavior is exactly preserved, while rising hydrodynamic moment smoothly withdraws transfer authority.
The candidate and durable guidance are both updated. I’m now checking the diff, parameter schema, workspace boundary, and the required non-CFD contract; I’ll repair any failure before handing it off.

The policy boundary passes. The guidance checker found a workspace-metadata defect: the rendered README marks the same optimizer parent as “prefill” twice, so it cannot resolve a unique assigned parent. I’m removing that duplicated listing, then rerunning the required checks; this does not alter the experiment or candidate.

The local checks now pass: notes/guidance semantics, solver boundary, nonempty candidate, and all 28 `params.FIELD` references match returned fields. I’m invoking the mandated independent check-runner now; it will not run CFD.

The configured check-runner role itself could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account. I’m preserving the same independent validation boundary by invoking a standard agent with the exact commands from that TOML; the checks and no-CFD restriction are unchanged.

Independent validation is complete: all three mandated checks pass, and no CFD was run. An additional state-grid check confirmed exact parent identity at low yaw load, active gate behavior at high load, finite outputs, and adherence to the acceleration envelope.

Produced exactly one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:254) adds a smooth yaw-load gate only to discretionary bidirectional work transfer.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:165) now incorporates the completed bidirectional, one-way, and unguarded results into a reusable lesson.

All mandated non-CFD checks passed: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, and editable boundary. A state-grid test also confirmed exact parent behavior at low load and bounded gate activation at high load. No CFD was run.

I also removed a duplicated parent-prefill entry from [README.md](README.md) that initially made the required guidance checker ambiguous.
